standard_prerequisites.name: The higher inductive-inductive Cauchy reals (R_C, closeness)
standard_prerequisites.statement: R_C is generated by rat : Q -> R_C together with lim on Cauchy approximations, simultaneously with the family u close_eps v generated by four constructors relating rational points and limits; the accompanying (R_C,close)-recursion principle produces f : R_C -> A from f(rat q), f(lim x), a separated family of relations on A and the four constructor conditions.
standard_prerequisites.use: The retained proof is one application of that principle, with A := R_C and the relation u ~_eps v := (u close_{L eps} v) set up at source lines 1080-1084.

standard_prerequisites.name: Lipschitz maps and Lipschitz constants
standard_prerequisites.statement: f : Q -> R_C is Lipschitz with constant L : Q+ when |q-r| < eps implies f(q) close_{L eps} f(r).
standard_prerequisites.use: Retained as context at source lines 1056-1069 and consumed in the rational/rational constructor case at line 1107.

standard_prerequisites.name: The extra clause of (R_C,close)-recursion
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function f produced by (R_C,close)-recursion satisfies u close_eps v -> f(u) ~_eps f(v); for the Cauchy reals this is equation 11.3.13 of the book.
standard_prerequisites.use: Source line 1118 quotes exactly this clause to conclude that the extension is Lipschitz with constant L; the clause lies outside the retained span and is declared as a non-load-bearing navigation pointer.

core_obligations: Choose the codomain R_C and the family of relations u ~_eps v := (u close_{L eps} v), and observe that the four recursion conditions on that relation amount to Lipschitzness of the extension on the four constructors of closeness (source lines 1080-1084 and 1104-1105).

Give the two recursion data: f-bar(rat q) := rat(f(q)) and f-bar(lim x) := lim(lam eps. f-bar(x_{eps/L})), checking first that lam eps. f-bar(x_{eps/L}) is a Cauchy approximation, which is exactly where the inductive hypothesis f-bar(x_delta) close_{L delta + L eps} f-bar(x_eps) is used (source lines 1085-1100).
Prove that the chosen relation is separated: if a close_{L eps} b for every eps : Q+ then a = b, by replacing L eps with an arbitrary eps (source line 1102).

Verify the four constructor conditions (rational/rational, limit/rational, rational/limit, limit/limit), each time turning the assumed close_{eps - delta} data into the L-scaled hypothesis and applying the matching constructor of closeness (source lines 1106-1116), and conclude both the computation rule f-bar(rat q) = f(q) and the Lipschitz constant from the recursion principle's extra clause (source lines 1117-1118).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix the codomain R_C and the relation u ~_eps v := (u close_{L eps} v) for the recursion.
Define f-bar on both constructors and justify the limit clause as a Cauchy approximation.
Check separatedness of the relation and reduce the remaining obligations to the four constructor cases.
Discharge the four constructor conditions, then read off the computation rule and the Lipschitz constant.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.3.15 at source lines 1073-1076: a Lipschitz f : Q -> R_C with constant L extends to f-bar : R_C -> R_C with the same constant and f-bar(rat q) = f(q). The proof is a single application of the (R_C,close)-recursion principle, but every obligation of that principle is discharged by hand: the extension is defined on both constructors (lines 1085-1095), the limit clause is legitimate only after showing that lam eps. f-bar(x_{eps/L}) is again a Cauchy approximation (lines 1097-1100), separatedness is checked against arbitrary pairs rather than against f-bar (line 1102), and each of the four constructor conditions converts a close_{eps-delta} hypothesis into the L-scaled close_{L eps - L delta} one before applying the matching constructor (lines 1106-1116). None of this eps/L bookkeeping is visible in the statement, so the work sits in the construction rather than in a citation.
